findings.issue_text: [BUG] `PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title(title)` in `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template` calls a method defined on `CommitContextIntegration`, not `PRCommentWorkflow`, raising AttributeError and breaking all merged-PR comments for the GitHub and GitLab PR bots.

[BUG] `fetch_error_details` in `project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py` uses `zip(error_ids, events.values())`, assuming `get_multi` returns values in the same order/count as `error_ids`; missing keys shift pairings and attribute error data to wrong event IDs in the Seer summary.

[ADVISORY] Migrations 0917 and 0920 are gutted to no-ops pointing to `0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py`, which is not in the diff; if 0921 doesn't exist, org saved searches are silently never converted, and environments where 0917/0920 ran have divergent state.

[ADVISORY] New `x-programs` entries in `devservices/config.yml` run consumer types (`eap-spans-subscription-results`, `subscription-results-eap-items`, `metrics-subscription-results`, `generic-metrics-subscription-results`) that aren't registered in the consumer-type registry, so `devservices up tracing` fails at container start.

[ADVISORY] The new `snuba-metrics` service in `devservices/config.yml` references `mode: containerized-metrics-dev`, which may not exist in pinned snuba master, causing `devservices up tracing` to fail launching the container.

[ADVISORY] `validate_timestamp` and its sibling validator in `browser_reporting_collector.py` have swapped docstrings and inverted error messages, misleading engineers and telling clients the wrong field to remove on a 422.

[ADVISORY] New imports and `get_filter_params` call in `project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py` have no test coverage; if `process_raw_response` returns a dict instead of a list, indexing `response[0].get(...)` crashes the endpoint with a 500.

[ADVISORY] PR title/description claims a Replays self-serve bulk delete system but the only related change is the max_segment_id None guard in src/sentry/replays/usecases/delete.py:87; no bulk-delete endpoint, usecase, permission gating, or self-serve path exists, so the PR ships a title that does not match any shipped functionality

[ADVISORY] Unrelated scope drift: DEFAULT_AUTOFIX_AUTOMATION_TUNING_DEFAULT changed from 'low' to 'off' in src/sentry/constants.py:724 and projectoptions/defaults.py:205, silently disabling autofix automation for every org/project relying on the default

[ADVISORY] Migrations 0917 and 0920 neutered to no-op return bodies based only on an in-code comment claiming they 'had an error and was never run', risking permanent out-of-sync environments and silently dropped org saved-search data if the claim is false

[ADVISORY] Complete rewrite of browser reporting ingestion endpoint (dataclass → DRF serializer, response-body changes) in src/sentry/issues/endpoints/browser_reporting_collector.py:21 with zero connection to replay deletion; public API validation semantics change hidden in an unrelated PR

[ADVISORY] New merged-PR comment feature (title truncation, environment enrichment) and template restructure across GitHub and Gitlab integrations in commit_context.py:577-608, unrelated user-facing feature where regressions surface as corrupted PR comments on customer repositories

[ADVISORY] New owner field handling in detector create/update validators mutates owner_user_id/owner_team_id without the audit-log update used for other fields, breaking the validator's invariant, and rides along unreviewed by workflow-engine owners

[ADVISORY] Refactor in delayed_workflow.py:354-420 hoisting get_slow_conditions_for_groups into the caller changes hot-path performance (one fetch instead of two) and adds new info-level logging with no stated requirement; failures affect workflow firing for all customers

[ADVISORY] Removal of ParameterizationRegexExperiment path and the grouping.experiments.parameterization.traceparent option is a silent public-surface change for out-of-tree callers/configs referencing it

[ADVISORY] Taskworker processing_deadline_duration tuning across deliver_webhooks.py:85,161,239 and check_auth.py:76 changes task deadline semantics (tasks killed at 30s/300s/120s) with no requirement; a webhook drain exceeding 300s now fails

[ADVISORY] Prompt-engineering changes to feedback-summarization LLM prompt including a new hard 55-word limit silently changes AI output for all feedback summaries and will not receive AI-feature review attention
[ADVISORY] NoiseConfig(ignore_limit=5) added to DBQueryInjectionVulnerabilityGroupType changes issue-creation/escalation behavior with no requirement stated and no test in the diff

[ADVISORY] New equations pass-through parameter on the logs top-events query and a new preprod analytics event wired into the assemble endpoint are new behavior-bearing public surface with no tests; the equations param is ships-inert until an out-of-diff consumer appears

[ADVISORY] Bulk frontend Flex/styled-div migration and button transition timing change (0.1s → 0.06s) are unreviewed visual/interaction changes to core components, with the timing change being a global button-animation behavior change with no requirement

[ADVISORY] New snuba-metrics service, four subscription-results consumers, and a full tracing dev-environment profile in devservices/config.yml grow the dev-environment footprint substantially for a feature unrelated to replay bulk deletion and create config drift risk

[ADVISORY] New error-context fetching logic in project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:67-118 lacks tests for fetch_error_details, which mis-zips error_ids with events.values() when nodestore returns misses; a regression breaks the summarize endpoint the PR was never supposed to touch

[BUG] In fetch_error_details, zip(error_ids, events.values()) misaligns pairings because get_multi returns a dict and values() only yields existing entries in dict order; a missing node shifts subsequent pairings so error A's title/message/timestamp gets attributed to error B's id. Correct shape is for event_id, data in zip(error_ids, map(events.get, node_ids)).

[BUG] In gen_request_data, timestamp-unit drift between replay-segment breadcrumb payloads (epoch-milliseconds) and nodestore event timestamps (epoch-seconds) means every error timestamp is smaller than every breadcrumb timestamp, so the interleave loop flushes all error log messages before the first breadcrumb instead of placing them chronologically.

[BUG] get_merged_pr_single_issue_template calls PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title(title), but _truncate_title is defined on CommitContextIntegration, not PRCommentWorkflow, raising AttributeError the first time a merged-PR comment is rendered for GitHub/GitLab and breaking PR bot comments entirely.

[ADVISORY] The analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...) call fires before the features.has("organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble") gate, so every request to a disabled org (including 403/404s, probes, and anonymous requests) emits an analytics event, corrupting the assemble funnel counts; move the record below the feature/permission gates.

[ADVISORY] The rewrite silently drops the subtitle (culprit) from merged-PR comment lines: the new MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE has no subtitle slot, and both GitHub and GitLab call sites deleted their format_comment_subtitle argument, leaving format_comment_subtitle as dead code if intentional, or losing the culprit string for users if not.

[ADVISORY] The endpoint issues an unconditional Snuba query_replay_instance (plus nodestore get_multi fan-out over all error IDs) before pagination begins, even when enable_error_context=false and across every per-page on_results callback, re-fetching the same replay row set once per page with no caching.

[BUG] fetch_error_details zips error_ids with events.values() from nodestore get_multi, which skips missing node_ids, shifting values and pairing every subsequent error with the wrong event's data when any requested event is absent.

[ADVISORY] The function reads data.get("message") directly off raw nodestore event data, but message is not a top-level key (it lives under logentry), so error context messages silently render as empty strings rather than failing loudly.

[ADVISORY] The default for sentry:autofix_automation_tuning changes from "low" to "off" for every org/project simultaneously with no feature flag, options migration, or per-org ramp, inside an unrelated PR titled 'Replays Self-Serve Bulk Delete System', silently flipping a user-visible automation default on deploy.

[ADVISORY] Migration 0917 (and 0920, same shape) body is replaced with a no-op return, so environments where the buggy migration already ran will have org saved searches silently skipped by 0921's re-run semantics, with no guard (e.g., checking for existing GroupSearchView rows) to catch the divergence.

[ADVISORY] The browser reporting collector rewrite replaces a permissive dataclass with a strict DRF serializer requiring user_agent as a mandatory CharField per report, but the newer spec draft moved user_agent to the envelope layer, so spec-compliant browsers get their entire report array rejected with 422 where the previous code accepted it.

[ADVISORY] get_merged_pr_single_issue_template is a staticmethod on CommitContextIntegration that reaches into PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title, adds a per-issue recommended-event fetch (nodestore/Snuba) inside the PR-comment path, and changes the rendered comment format (bullet style, dropped culprit subtitle, added environment, 50-char title truncation) without tests covering the new template rendering.

[ADVISORY] The endpoint's GET unconditionally runs a Snuba query_replay_instance call plus nodestore get_multi before pagination, gated only by an undocumented ad-hoc query param enable_error_context (no feature flag, no options entry), so the new error-context behavior cannot be disabled in production without a code deploy.

[ADVISORY] The PR's stated objective ('Replays Self-Serve Bulk Delete System') no longer describes its contents — it ships a workflow-engine refactor, a grouping-parameterization experiment removal (including unregistered option grouping.experiments.parameterization.traceparent, leaving stored option values that validate against nothing), noise-config changes, task deadline changes, a feedback-summary prompt rewrite, and dozens of frontend Flex migrations with no acceptance trace tying them to the stated intent.

[ADVISORY] New logger.warning writes the full raw browser report body (including URL with potential PII/tokens from query strings) to logs on an unauthenticated, CORS-open endpoint, creating an unredacted PII leak into log storage and a log-flooding vector; the debug value could be retained by logging only the report type and serializer errors instead of raw_report

[ADVISORY] The 422 response body echoes serializer.errors back to the caller, and DRF error details can embed the offending input value (e.g. the rejected URL), creating an open reflection/oracle surface on the unauthenticated, CORS-enabled endpoint; should return a static error string and keep details in logs

[BUG] In project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py ~87 fetch_error_details, zip(error_ids, events.values()) pairs error IDs with nodestore results positionally, but nodestore.backend.get_multi returns a dict whose values are in node-id iteration order and silently omits missing keys — when any node is missing, subsequent (event_id, data) pairs are misaligned, attributing one error's title/message/timestamp to a different error ID in the Seer summary.

[BUG] In browser_reporting_collector.py:46-58 validate_timestamp / validate_age, mutual-exclusion checks use truthiness (if self.initial_data.get("age")), so age=0 together with a timestamp (or timestamp=0 with age) passes both validators, producing a validated report carrying both spec-conflicting fields.

[ADVISORY] In browser_reporting_collector.py:41-46, both age and timestamp are required=False with no validate enforcing one-of, so a report with neither field validates cleanly; the endpoint accepts reports with no time anchoring at all, and future consumers assuming a time field exists hit KeyError/None silently.

[ADVISORY] In commit_context.py ~600 get_merged_pr_single_issue_template, a @staticmethod on CommitContextIntegration is invoked as self.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template from GitHubPRCommentWorkflow/GitlabPRCommentWorkflow and internally calls PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title — a forward dependency on a later-defined, differently-based class — so refactoring PRCommentWorkflow or removing the misplaced static breaks merged-PR comment rendering in both integrations.

[ADVISORY] Editing already-shipped migration files 0917/0920 into no-ops based on the unverified claim they were never run risks environments that did record them as applied skipping conversion semantics; correctness depends on 0921 being idempotent, which is not verified in the diff

[ADVISORY] The retired 0920 body filtered owner_id__isnull=False, silently dropping organization-visibility saved searches with no owner from conversion; the replacement 0921 may carry the same filter and org-level saved searches owned by deleted users could be permanently lost

[BUG] get_merged_pr_single_issue_template calls PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title(title), but _truncate_title is a @staticmethod on CommitContextIntegration, not PRCommentWorkflow; since they are sibling ABCs using composition, this raises AttributeError for every merged-PR comment from GitHub and GitLab integrations

[BUG] In project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py (fetch_error_details, ~line 90-100), `zip(error_ids, events.values())` mispairs error IDs with nodestore data: when a node_id is missing, events.values() is shorter than error_ids, so every subsequent data is zipped with the wrong event_id and events after the truncation point are silently dropped, causing the Seer summary to report error titles/messages attributed to the wrong error IDs. Fix by iterating keys with events.get(Event.generate_node_id(project_id, eid)).

[BUG] In commit_context.py (get_merged_pr_single_issue_template, ~line 595), `PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title(title)` references `_truncate_title`, which is defined as a @staticmethod on `CommitContextIntegration`, not on `PRCommentWorkflow` (which inherits from OpenPRCommentWorkflow/ABC), raising AttributeError the first time a merged-PR comment body is built, crashing the bot comment posting and failing the whole comment job.

[BUG] In browser_reporting_collector.py (attempts field, ~line 40), `attempts = serializers.IntegerField(min_value=1)` rejects `attempts: 0`, the value browsers send on the first delivery attempt per the Reporting API spec, so nearly all first-attempt reports get a 422 and are dropped.

[ADVISORY] In browser_reporting_collector.py (validate_timestamp/validate_age, ~lines 44-55), the cross-field validators only reject the both-present case; a report with neither `age` nor `timestamp` passes validation, so degenerate payloads are accepted and data-quality consumers cannot distinguish spec-compliant from non-compliant payloads.

[ADVISORY] In browser_reporting_collector.py, both error messages state the inverse of the check being performed (e.g., "If timestamp is present, age must be absent" is raised when validating timestamp and age is present).

[ADVISORY] In project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py (get, new pre-pagination queries), the endpoint runs a Snuba query_replay_instance query plus a nodestore get_multi on every paginated page request even though the error data is page-independent, and analyze_recording_segments re-injects the full error_events list into every page's log stream, duplicating error context per page, inflating latency and Seer token usage.

In BaseDetectorTypeValidator.update(), the validator incorrectly updates instance.type using validated_data.get('detector_type') instead of validated_data.get('type').

Using zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes the get_multi result preserves the input order; dict value order is not guaranteed to match error_ids, so event data can be paired with the wrong ID (missing nodes also shift alignment).
Hardcoded empty data passed to TableWidgetVisualization causes it to always render an empty table instead of displaying actual results when the feature flag is enabled.

Validation logic incorrectly uses .get('timestamp'), which treats a timestamp of 0 as absent. It should directly check 'timestamp' in self.initial_data to ensure proper field presence detection, preventing both 'age=0' and 'timestamp' from passing mutual-exclusion validation.

Analytics events are recorded before the feature flag check, resulting in analytics being logged for all requests, including those that return 404 due to the feature being disabled. This can lead to misleading analytics data.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Migrations 0917 and 0920 are gutted to no-ops pointing to `0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py`, which is not in the diff; if 0921 doesn't exist, org saved searches are silently never converted, and environments where 0917/0920 ran have divergent state.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes migrations 0917 and 0920 to immediate no-ops with comments pointing to a replacement migration `0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py`. That replacement file is not included in this diff, so from the diff alone it’s impossible to verify that the conversion logic still exists/applies, and it’s a reasonable review concern to confirm 0921 exists and handles any prior-state scenarios. However, the finding’s claim that 0921 might not exist / that 0917/0920 previously ran and could cause divergent state cannot be proven from the diff alone (the comments assert they were never run).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] New `x-programs` entries in `devservices/config.yml` run consumer types (`eap-spans-subscription-results`, `subscription-results-eap-items`, `metrics-subscription-results`, `generic-metrics-subscription-results`) that aren't registered in the consumer-type registry, so `devservices up tracing` fails at container start.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add new `x-programs` entries in `devservices/config.yml` for the listed consumers, but it does not show any “consumer-type registry” or any registration mechanism to verify the claim that these consumer types are unregistered or that `devservices up tracing` will fail at container start. That failure mode depends on code/config not present in the diff, so the finding cannot be confirmed from what’s shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new `snuba-metrics` service in `devservices/config.yml` references `mode: containerized-metrics-dev`, which may not exist in pinned snuba master, causing `devservices up tracing` to fail launching the container.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce a new devservices service `snuba-metrics` with `remote.mode: containerized-metrics-dev` (in `devservices/config.yml`). Whether that mode actually exists/works in the referenced external repo (`getsentry/snuba` on `master`) is not verifiable from this PR diff alone, but it is a concrete integration risk introduced by the change (a potentially invalid mode string could break `devservices up tracing`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `validate_timestamp` and its sibling validator in `browser_reporting_collector.py` have swapped docstrings and inverted error messages, misleading engineers and telling clients the wrong field to remove on a 422.

adjudication.rationale: In `BrowserReportSerializer` the field-level validators match their logic and error messages: `validate_timestamp` raises only when `age` is also present (`"If timestamp is present, age must be absent"`), and `validate_age` raises only when `timestamp` is also present (`"If age is present, timestamp must be absent"`). The docstrings are consistent with this mutual-exclusion rule; nothing in the diff shows swapped docstrings or inverted client guidance.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] New imports and `get_filter_params` call in `project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py` have no test coverage; if `process_raw_response` returns a dict instead of a list, indexing `response[0].get(...)` crashes the endpoint with a 500.

adjudication.rationale: The diff *does* add tests covering the new replay summarize logic and error-context behavior in `tests/sentry/replays/test_project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py` (e.g., `test_get_with_error`, `test_get_with_error_context_disabled`, updated `test_get_request_data`). The claim of “no test coverage” is therefore false. The potential 500 via `response[0].get(...)` would only occur if `process_raw_response(...)` can return a dict, but the diff does not show that return type or any change to `process_raw_response`, so that crash scenario cannot be verified from this PR diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] PR title/description claims a Replays self-serve bulk delete system but the only related change is the max_segment_id None guard in src/sentry/replays/usecases/delete.py:87; no bulk-delete endpoint, usecase, permission gating, or self-serve path exists, so the PR ships a title that does not match any shipped functionality

adjudication.rationale: The finding hinges on the PR title/description claiming a “Replays self-serve bulk delete system,” but the PR title/description is not present in the provided diff, so this mismatch cannot be verified from the diff alone. The diff does show a replay-deletion-related change (guarding `max_segment_id is None` in `src/sentry/replays/usecases/delete.py`) and a corresponding test adjustment, but whether that contradicts the PR’s stated scope is not determinable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Unrelated scope drift: DEFAULT_AUTOFIX_AUTOMATION_TUNING_DEFAULT changed from 'low' to 'off' in src/sentry/constants.py:724 and projectoptions/defaults.py:205, silently disabling autofix automation for every org/project relying on the default

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes the default autofix automation tuning from "low" to "off" in both `src/sentry/constants.py` (DEFAULT_AUTOFIX_AUTOMATION_TUNING_DEFAULT) and the registered project option default in `src/sentry/projectoptions/defaults.py` (`sentry:autofix_automation_tuning`). Tests are updated to expect "off" as the default, indicating an intentional behavior change rather than an accidental defect. However, it is a significant default-behavior change (effectively disabling autofix automation for projects relying on defaults) and the finding's scope-drift concern is grounded in what the diff does.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Migrations 0917 and 0920 neutered to no-op return bodies based only on an in-code comment claiming they 'had an error and was never run', risking permanent out-of-sync environments and silently dropped org saved-search data if the claim is false

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes both migration functions (0917_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views.py and 0920_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_revised.py) from performing SavedSearch -> GroupSearchView conversion to a bare `return`, justified only by an inline comment (“had an error and was never run”). The PR also deletes the test for 0917. From the diff alone we cannot verify the claim that these migrations were never run everywhere, and if that assumption is wrong (or if the referenced 0921 migration doesn’t fully cover all cases), this could leave some environments not migrating org saved-search data as originally intended. This is a concrete, diff-grounded risk, but not a provable defect without knowing migration history / what 0921 does.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Complete rewrite of browser reporting ingestion endpoint (dataclass → DRF serializer, response-body changes) in src/sentry/issues/endpoints/browser_reporting_collector.py:21 with zero connection to replay deletion; public API validation semantics change hidden in an unrelated PR

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a substantial rewrite of `src/sentry/issues/endpoints/browser_reporting_collector.py`: it replaces the `BrowserReport` dataclass + `Literal` typing with a DRF `Serializer`, changes validation behavior (e.g., new required field checks, `age`/`timestamp` mutual-exclusion validation), and changes error responses from empty `HttpResponse(422)`/`HttpResponse(404)` to DRF `Response` objects that can include a JSON body with `{error, details}`. This is a real, diff-grounded scope/API-semantics change and is independent of the replay deletion changes also present in the PR, but it is not inherently a verifiable defect from the diff alone (tests were updated/added accordingly).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] New merged-PR comment feature (title truncation, environment enrichment) and template restructure across GitHub and Gitlab integrations in commit_context.py:577-608, unrelated user-facing feature where regressions surface as corrupted PR comments on customer repositories

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/integrations/source_code_management/commit_context.py`, the newly added `CommitContextIntegration.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template()` calls `PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title(title)`, but `_truncate_title` is defined on `CommitContextIntegration` (as `_truncate_title`) and the diff shows no corresponding `_truncate_title` on `PRCommentWorkflow`. This mismatch is a concrete, diff-visible correctness issue that can raise at runtime when building merged-PR comments (GitHub/GitLab now call `self.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template(...)`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] New owner field handling in detector create/update validators mutates owner_user_id/owner_team_id without the audit-log update used for other fields, breaking the validator's invariant, and rides along unreviewed by workflow-engine owners

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/workflow_engine/endpoints/validators/base/detector.py`, the serializer `update()`/`create()` methods mutate detector fields (e.g., `instance.name`, `instance.type`, and now `owner_user_id`/`owner_team_id`) but the diff does not show any audit-log calls for *any* of these field mutations. The finding asserts there is an existing “audit-log update used for other fields” invariant that the new owner handling violates, but that behavior is not evidenced in the shown changes. The additional claim about being “unreviewed by workflow-engine owners” is process-oriented and not verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Refactor in delayed_workflow.py:354-420 hoisting get_slow_conditions_for_groups into the caller changes hot-path performance (one fetch instead of two) and adds new info-level logging with no stated requirement; failures affect workflow firing for all customers

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/delayed_workflow.py`, the diff hoists `get_slow_conditions_for_groups(...)` into `process_delayed_workflows` and threads the result into both `get_condition_query_groups(...)` and `get_groups_to_fire(...)`, eliminating the prior duplicated fetches inside those helpers. This is a behavior/architecture change that can affect performance characteristics (now one fetch per task rather than potentially two) and it also introduces new `logger.info("delayed_workflow.no_slow_condition_groups", ...)` logging that could be noisy depending on how often that mismatch occurs. The finding’s claim about “failures affect workflow firing for all customers” is speculative from the diff alone (no new failure mode is clearly introduced beyond possible KeyError if mappings diverge), so it’s not a verifiable bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Removal of ParameterizationRegexExperiment path and the grouping.experiments.parameterization.traceparent option is a silent public-surface change for out-of-tree callers/configs referencing it

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] New logger.warning writes the full raw browser report body (including URL with potential PII/tokens from query strings) to logs on an unauthenticated, CORS-open endpoint, creating an unredacted PII leak into log storage and a log-flooding vector; the debug value could be retained by logging only the report type and serializer errors instead of raw_report

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In browser_reporting_collector.py:46-58 validate_timestamp / validate_age, mutual-exclusion checks use truthiness (if self.initial_data.get("age")), so age=0 together with a timestamp (or timestamp=0 with age) passes both validators, producing a validated report carrying both spec-conflicting fields.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] In browser_reporting_collector.py:41-46, both age and timestamp are required=False with no validate enforcing one-of, so a report with neither field validates cleanly; the endpoint accepts reports with no time anchoring at all, and future consumers assuming a time field exists hit KeyError/None silently.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py (fetch_error_details, ~line 90-100), `zip(error_ids, events.values())` mispairs error IDs with nodestore data: when a node_id is missing, events.values() is shorter than error_ids, so every subsequent data is zipped with the wrong event_id and events after the truncation point are silently dropped, causing the Seer summary to report error titles/messages attributed to the wrong error IDs. Fix by iterating keys with events.get(Event.generate_node_id(project_id, eid)).

adjudication.rationale: In `fetch_error_details` (new code in `project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py`), it builds `node_ids`, calls `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` (a dict keyed by node_id), then constructs results via `for event_id, data in zip(error_ids, events.values())`. This loses the key association and can misattribute data to the wrong `event_id` if `get_multi` omits missing keys or returns a dict whose `values()` order doesn’t align 1:1 with `error_ids`. The suggested fix (lookup by generated node_id per error_id) would preserve correct pairing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In browser_reporting_collector.py (attempts field, ~line 40), `attempts = serializers.IntegerField(min_value=1)` rejects `attempts: 0`, the value browsers send on the first delivery attempt per the Reporting API spec, so nearly all first-attempt reports get a 422 and are dropped.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly sets `attempts = serializers.IntegerField(min_value=1)` in `BrowserReportSerializer`, and the new tests explicitly assert `attempts: 0` is rejected with a 422. However, the claim that “browsers send attempts: 0 on first delivery attempt per the Reporting API spec” (and thus that “nearly all first-attempt reports get dropped”) cannot be verified from the diff itself; it depends on external spec behavior not shown here. This is therefore a concrete, diff-grounded compatibility concern, but not a verifiable defect from the PR alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] In browser_reporting_collector.py (validate_timestamp/validate_age, ~lines 44-55), the cross-field validators only reject the both-present case; a report with neither `age` nor `timestamp` passes validation, so degenerate payloads are accepted and data-quality consumers cannot distinguish spec-compliant from non-compliant payloads.

adjudication.rationale: In `BrowserReportSerializer`, both `age` and `timestamp` are `required=False`. The only cross-field checks are `validate_timestamp` (errors if `age` is present) and `validate_age` (errors if `timestamp` is present). If neither field is provided, neither validator runs and the serializer will accept the report as valid, meaning payloads missing both spec-specific fields pass validation. This matches the finding’s claim that degenerate payloads are accepted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] In browser_reporting_collector.py, both error messages state the inverse of the check being performed (e.g., "If timestamp is present, age must be absent" is raised when validating timestamp and age is present).

adjudication.rationale: In `BrowserReportSerializer`, `validate_timestamp` only runs when `timestamp` is provided, so the error message “If timestamp is present, age must be absent” is consistent with the situation where both `timestamp` (being validated) and `age` (found in `initial_data`) are present. Likewise `validate_age` only runs when `age` is provided, and its message matches that case. The diff even adds a test (`test_mixed_fields`) asserting these exact messages for mixed `age`+`timestamp`, indicating this wording is intentional, not inverted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] In project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py (get, new pre-pagination queries), the endpoint runs a Snuba query_replay_instance query plus a nodestore get_multi on every paginated page request even though the error data is page-independent, and analyze_recording_segments re-injects the full error_events list into every page's log stream, duplicating error context per page, inflating latency and Seer token usage.

adjudication.rationale: In `ProjectReplaySummarizeBreadcrumbsEndpoint.get`, the new code performs page-independent work (Snuba `query_replay_instance` + `process_raw_response` to get `error_ids`, then `fetch_error_details()` which does `nodestore.backend.get_multi`) before calling `self.paginate(...)`. Because pagination is driven by separate HTTP requests for each page, this same Snuba + nodestore work will be repeated on every page request. Additionally, `on_results=functools.partial(analyze_recording_segments, error_events)` passes the full `error_events` list into `analyze_recording_segments` for every page, and `gen_request_data(...)` yields any remaining errors after processing the page’s segments, so the same error context can be re-injected across pages. This is a concrete performance/architecture concern (latency / Seer payload size), not a correctness defect visible in the diff.
